title: Critical Apache HttpComponents Flaw Allows Server Impersonation in MITM Attacks
content_md: A critical vulnerability in Apache HttpComponents Client could allow attackers to impersonate trusted servers during man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks when applications use the asynchronous HttpClient implementation. Tracked as CVE-2026-71290, the issue stems from improper TLS hostname verification in Apache HttpComponents Client versions 5.4 through 5.6.3. The vulnerability affects applications configured with HostnameVerificationPolicy#BUILTIN while using the async version of Apache HttpClient. Critical Apache HttpComponents Flaw Although the setting is intended to enforce hostname validation during a TLS handshake , it reportedly has no effect in vulnerable async configurations. TLS hostname verification is a critical control that confirms whether the hostname requested by a client matches the identity listed in the server’s TLS certificate. Without this validation, a certificate that is otherwise valid but issued for an unrelated domain may be accepted by the client. An attacker capable of intercepting and modifying traffic between an affected application and its intended destination could exploit this behavior. By presenting a legitimate TLS certificate for a different domain, the attacker may successfully impersonate the target server to the vulnerable async client. This could expose API requests, authentication tokens, session data, credentials, and other sensitive information transmitted over HTTPS connections.
